title: LinkedIn to add AI slop report feature that could train better AI slop
excerpt: Over 40 percent of longform posts on LinkedIn are completely AI-generated, a recent study found.
content_html:
LinkedIn will soon enable users to flag posts which appear to be "AI slop." However, the career-focused social media platform won't be using this data to remove or even discourage AI-generated posts. Rather, it appears the company will use the feedback to train its own algorithms. 

The upcoming update was announced on Thursday, with LinkedIn's chief product officer Hari Srinivasan stating that AI slop is a "top priority" for the company.

"We are ramping [up] the ability for members to tell us if they believe a post or comment seems like AI slop," Srinivasan wrote in a post on the platform. "Slop is hard to define and the definition changes; this lets us tune our models and make better feeds."

It's unclear exactly what he means by making LinkedIn's feeds "better," but it's unlikely that it involves the complete absence of generative AI. Srinivasan went on to express the belief that AI-generated posts and AI slop are not synonymous, arguing that people use AI to "refine their thoughts."

As such, flagging AI-generated posts on LinkedIn could potentially deprioritise such content. Srinivasan further stated that LinkedIn is adding new classifiers to help identify AI slop and will reduce the amount shown in suggested content. However, it seems likely that the data will also help train LinkedIn's generative AI, so that its AI-generated content is less detectable.

Mashable Light Speed

LinkedIn previously offered a relatively unpopular "AI-powered writing tool" that allowed users to generate posts for the platform. This feature was removed alongside Thursday's announcement, with Srinivasan stating that it will be replaced with a proofreading tool. 

Even so, it's probable that the upcoming feature will also use generative AI, with Srinivasan specifically noting that it will not change the users' voice. The platform also still offers AI-generated suggestions for users updating their profiles or company pages.

LinkedIn's AI slop report feature doesn't just have the potential to help the platform refine its own algorithms either. Srinivasan noted that users who publish AI-generated content on LinkedIn will also be informed when others tag their posts as AI slop, offering the feedback so they can work on making their AI-generated content sound more "authentic."

"For anyone who shares content, we will test a way to privately flag, in your analytics dashboard, when members feel your post may have come off as inauthentic or heavy use of AI," wrote Srinivasan. ""[W]e believe [AI users] want to know when they sound inauthentic…. [W]e want members to get feedback from real humans on what sounds authentic — not just have an AI detector review it and get it wrong."

Earlier this month, AI detection tool Pangram published a study that found over 40 percent of longform posts on LinkedIn were completely AI-generated.

content_html_zh:
LinkedIn 很快将允许用户标记看似“AI 垃圾”的帖子。 然而，以职业为中心的社交媒体平台不会使用这些数据来删除甚至阻止人工智能生成的帖子。 相反，该公司似乎将利用这些反馈来训练自己的算法。

周四宣布了即将到来的更新，LinkedIn 首席产品官 Hari Srinivasan 表示，人工智能技术是该公司的“首要任务”。

斯里尼瓦桑在该平台上的一篇帖子中写道：“我们正在增强会员告诉我们他们是否认为某条帖子或评论看起来像是人工智能废话的能力。” “坡度很难定义，并且定义会发生变化；这让我们能够调整模型并做出更好的反馈。”

目前尚不清楚他所说的让 LinkedIn 的信息流变得“更好”到底是什么意思，但这不太可能意味着完全不使用生成式人工智能。 斯里尼瓦桑接着表示，人工智能生成的帖子和人工智能垃圾并不是同义词，他认为人们使用人工智能来“完善他们的想法”。

因此，在 LinkedIn 上标记人工智能生成的帖子可能会降低此类内容的优先级。 斯里尼瓦桑进一步表示，LinkedIn 正在添加新的分类器，以帮助识别人工智能溢出，并将减少建议内容中显示的数量。 然而，这些数据似乎也将有助于训练 LinkedIn 的生成式人工智能，从而使其人工智能生成的内容不易被检测到。

可混搭光速

LinkedIn此前提供了一款相对不受欢迎的“人工智能驱动的写作工具”，允许用户为该平台生成帖子。 该功能在周四的公告中被删除，斯里尼瓦桑表示它将被校对工具取代。

即便如此，即将推出的功能很可能也将使用生成式人工智能，斯里尼瓦桑特别指出，它不会改变用户的声音。 该平台还为更新个人资料或公司页面的用户提供人工智能生成的建议。

LinkedIn 的人工智能溢出报告功能不仅有潜力帮助该平台完善自己的算法。 斯里尼瓦桑指出，当其他人将他们的帖子标记为人工智能废话时，在 LinkedIn 上发布人工智能生成内容的用户也会收到通知，并提供反馈，以便他们可以努力让人工智能生成的内容听起来更“真实”。

斯里尼瓦桑写道：“对于任何分享内容的人，当会员认为你的帖子可能不真实或大量使用人工智能时，我们将在你的分析仪表板中测试一种私下标记的方法。” “”[W]我们相信[人工智能用户]想知道他们什么时候听起来不真实……我们希望会员能够从真实的人类那里获得关于听起来真实的反馈——而不仅仅是让人工智能探测器对其进行审查并出错。”

本月早些时候，人工智能检测工具 Pangram 发布了一项研究，发现 LinkedIn 上超过 40% 的长篇帖子完全是人工智能生成的。
